main.content:
==English==
[[File:Cannon Child Development Center 120125-F-YG475-143.jpg|thumb|Children playing with toys ''(sense 1)'' ]]

===Etymology===
{{ety|en|:inh|enm:pleyen<id:play>|enm:pleye|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|pleyen|pos=verb}} and {{inh|en|enm|pleye|pos=noun}}, from {{inh|en|ang|plegian}} and {{m|ang|plegan}}, {{m|ang|plagian||to play, exercise, etc.}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*plehan||to care about, be concerned with}} and {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*plegōn||to engage, move}}, of uncertain origin.

{{col-top|2|cognates and related terms}}
Cognate with {{cog|sco|play||to act or move briskly, cause to move, stir}}, {{cog|stq|pleegje||to look after, care for, maintain}}, {{cog|fy|pleegje}}, {{m|fy|pliigje||to commit, perform, bedrive}}, {{cog|dum|pleyen}} {{gloss|"to dance, leap for joy, rejoice, be glad"; compare Modern {{cog|nl|pleien||to play a particular children's game}}}}, {{cog|nl|plegen||to commit, bedrive, practice}}, {{cog|de|pflegen||to care for, be concerned with, attend to, tend}}. Related also to {{cog|ang|plēon||to risk, endanger}}. More at {{l|en|plight}}, {{l|en|pledge}}.
{{col-bottom}}

The noun is from {{inh|en|enm|pleye}}, from {{inh|en|ang|plæġ}}, {{m|ang|plega}}, {{m|ang|plæġa||play, quick [[motion]], [[movement]], exercise; (athletic) [[sport]], [[game]]; festivity, [[drama]]; [[battle]]; gear for games, an implement for a game; clapping with the hands, applause}}, deverbative of {{m|ang|plegian||to play}}; see above.

===Pronunciation===
{{enPR|plā}}
* {{IPA|en|/pleɪ̯/ [pɫ̥eɪ̯ ~ pʰɫeɪ̯]|a=GA}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-play.ogg|a=California|IPA=[pɫ̥e̞e̯]}}
* {{IPA|en|/ple(j)/|a=Indic}}
* {{rhymes|en|eɪ|s=1}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[act]] in a [[manner]] such that one has [[fun]]; to [[engage]] in [[activity|activities]] [[expressly]] for the [[purpose]] of [[recreation]] or [[entertainment]].
#: {{ux|en|The children '''played''' in the park.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2001|author=Annabelle Sabloff|title=Reordering the Natural World|publisher=Univ. of Toronto Press|page=83|passage=A youngster{{...}}listed some of the things his pet did not do<!--''...''-->:{{...}}go on vacation, '''play''' in the same way that he did with his friends, and so on.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive|especially with 'with'; see also [[play with]]}} To [[toy]] or [[trifle]]; to [[act]] with [[levity]] or [[thoughtlessness]]; to be [[careless]].
#: {{ux|en|Don't '''play''' with your food!}}
#: {{ux|en|He's just '''playing''' with her affections.}}
#* {{RQ:Temple Miscellanea|part=3|page=167|passage=Thus Men are apt to '''play''' with their Healths and their Lives as they do with their Cloaths: [...]}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|intransitive}} To [[perform]] in (a [[sport]]); to [[participate]] in (a [[game]]).
#: {{hyper|en|try}}
#: {{hypo|en|replay}}
#: {{ux|en|He '''plays''' on three teams.}}
#: {{ux|en|Who's '''playing''' now?}}
#: {{ux|en|'''play''' football, '''play''' sports, '''play''' games}}
## {{n-g|Specifying a particular sporting role or position.}} <!-- unclear that this is truly transitive -->
##: {{ux|en|He '''plays''' left back for Mudchester Rovers}}
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[compete]] [[against]], in a [[game]].
##: {{ux|en|We're '''playing''' one of the top teams in the next round.}}
## {{lb|en|transitive|in the scoring of games and sports}} To be the [[opposing]] [[score]] to.
##: {{ux|en|Look at the score now ... 23 '''plays''' 8!}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To contend or fight using weapons, both as practice or in real life-or-death [[combat]]s; to engage in martial games; to [[joust]]; to [[fence#Verb|fence]]
# {{lb|en|intransitive|copulative}} To [[act]] or [[behave]] in a stated way.
#: {{ux|en|to '''play''' safe, to '''play''' fair, to '''play''' dirty}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Merchant of Venice|act=I|scene=ii|passage=His mother '''played''' false with a smith.}}
#* {{quote-song|en|lyricist=w:Stevie Nicks|composer=w:Fleetwood Mac|authorlabel=no|title={{w|Dreams (Fleetwood Mac song)|Dreams}}|album={{w|Rumours (album)|Rumours}}|year=1977|artist=w:Stevie Nicks|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PgagPdVM7bk|text=Now here you go again, you say you want your freedom / Well, who am I to keep you down? / It's only right that you should '''play''' the way you feel it / But listen carefully to the sound of your loneliness}}
## To [[give]] a [[false]] [[appearance]] of [[being]]; to [[pretend]] to [[be]].
##: {{ux|en|He [[play dumb|'''plays''' dumb]], but actually he's very clever.}}
##: {{ux|en|Don't '''play''' the innocent with us.}}
##* {{RQ:Scott Ivanhoe|passage=Thou canst '''play''' the rational if thou wilt.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=1985|author=Sharon S. Brehm|title=Intimate Relationships
|passage='''Playing''' hard to get is not the same as slamming the door in someone's face.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=1996|author=Michael P. Malone|title=James J Hill: Empire Builder of the Northwest
|passage=Now, surveying his final link, he had the nice advantage of being able to '''play''' coy with established port cities that desperately wanted his proven railroad.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=2003|author=John U. Ogbu|title=Black American Students in an Affluent Suburb: A Study of Academic Disengagement|page=194
|passage=Instead, they '''played''' dumb, remained silent, and did their classwork.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[act]] as (the [[indicated]] [[role]]).
#: {{ux|en|Stop '''playing''' the fool.}}
#: {{ux|en|No part of the brain '''plays''' the role of permanent memory.}}
## To [[portray]] (a [[character]]) in (a [[film]] or [[theatre]]).
##: {{ux|en|Who '''played'''  Scarlett O'Hara in 'Gone with the Wind'?}}
##* '''1984''', {{w|Chris Robinson (actor)|Chris Robinson}}, commercial for Vicks Formula 44:
##*: {{quote|en|I'm not a doctor, but I do '''play''' one on TV.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|intransitive}} ''To [[produce]] [[sound]] (especially [[music]]), [[moving picture]]s{{,}} or [[theatrical]] [[performance]].''<!-- Bearing in mind the large number of combinations of types of subject and object for these senses, this section aims to keep the number of separate definitions manageable, rather than necessarily listing and defining every possibility completely rigorously. -->
## {{lb|en|transitive|intransitive|especially|of a|person}} To produce music using a [[musical instrument]].
##: {{syn|en|cook|q1=intransitive|jam|q2=intransitive|Thesaurus:play music}}
##: {{ux|en|I'll '''play''' the piano and you sing.}}
##: {{ux|en|Can you '''play''' an instrument?}}
##: {{ux|en|I've practiced the piano off and on, but I still can't '''play''' very well.}}
## {{lb|en|intransitive|of a musical instrument}} To produce music.
##: {{ux|en|This piano '''plays''' out of tune.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=2007|author=Dan Erlewine|title=Guitar Player Repair Guide|isbn=0879309210|page=220
|passage=If your guitar '''plays''' well on fretted strings but annoys you on the open ones, the nut's probably worn out.}}
## {{lb|en|transitive|of a person}} To [[operate]] (a [[device]] or [[media]]) so as to [[cause]] sound (especially music) or moving pictures to be produced.
##: {{ux|en|You can '''play''' the DVD now.}}
##: {{ux|en|Don't '''play''' your radio so loud!}}
##: {{ux|en|'''Play''' the audio clip to hear how the word is pronounced.}}
## {{lb|en|transitive|usually of a person}} To {{l|en|render|id=interpret}} (a musical [[title]], [[compositional]] [[style]], [[film]] title, etc.) using a musical instrument or device.
##: {{ux|en|Do you know how to '''play''' Für Elise on the piano?}}
##: {{ux|en|We especially like to '''play''' jazz together.}}
##: {{ux|en|She keeps '''playing''' 'Achy Breaky Heart' over and over again on her stereo.}}
## {{lb|en|transitive|intransitive|of a device, media, broadcast, etc.}} To [[emit]] or [[relay]] sound (especially music) or moving pictures; {{lb|en|of a device}} to [[operate]] [[media]].
##: {{ux|en|The juke box is '''playing ''' our favourite song.}}
##: {{ux|en|The radio was '''playing ''' in the background.}}
##: {{ux|en|This DVD is scratched and won't '''play'''.}}
##: {{ux|en|Channel 9 is '''playing''' that old comedy series again.}}
##: {{ux|en|My cassette player won't '''play''' this worn-out old tape.}}
## {{lb|en|intransitive|of a|theatrical performance|film|or|music}} To be [[perform]]ed, [[reproduce]]d{{,}} or [[show]]n.
##: {{ux|en|His latest film is '''playing''' in the local theatre tomorrow.}}
##: {{ux|en|Some kind of lounge music was '''playing''' in the background.}}
## {{lb|en|transitive|of a|theatrical company|or|band|etc.}} To [[perform]] or give performances in or at (a [[venue]] or [[location]]).
##: {{ux|en|The band is '''playing''' large arenas nationwide.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=2008|title=My Life: From Normandy to Hockeytown|page=30|isbn=0966412087
|passage=I got a hold of Louis (Satchmo) Armstrong's agent and I explained to him on the phone that, "I know you're '''playing''' London on Wednesday night. Why don't you come and '''play''' the Arena in Windsor on Saturday night?"}}
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To act or perform (a play).
##: {{ux|en|to '''play''' a comedy}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|intransitive}} To [[move]] [[briskly]], [[sweepingly]], [[back and forth]], in a [[directed]] [[manner]], etc.
## To move in a [[light]] or [[brisk]] manner.
##: {{ux|en|The fountain '''plays'''.}}
##: {{ux|en|The leaves '''played''' in the wind.}}
##* {{RQ:Pope Essay on Man|passage=All fame is foreign but of true desert,  /  '''Plays''' round the head, but comes not to the heart.}}
## To move so as to [[fall upon]] or [[sweep]] [[across]] something, or to [[direct]] or [[operate]] (something) in such a manner.
##: {{ux|en|The torch beam '''played''' around the room.}}
##: {{ux|en|They '''played''' the jet of water onto the seat of the fire.}}
##: {{ux|en|to '''play''' cannon upon a fortification}}
##* {{RQ:Addison Cato|page=60|passage=[T]he ſetting Sun / '''Plays''' on their ſhining Arms and burniſh'd Helmets, / And cover's all the Field vvith Gleams of Fire.}}
##* {{RQ:Ferguson Zollenstein|I|passage=The colonel and his sponsor made a queer contrast: Greystone [the sponsor] long and stringy, with a face that seemed as if a cold wind was eternally '''playing''' on it.}}
## To move in an [[alternating]] or [[reciprocal]] manner; to move [[to and fro]].
##* {{RQ:Shakespeare Taming of the Shrew|act=Induction|scene=ii|passage=the waving sedges '''play''' with wind}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=1705|author={{w|George Cheyne (physician) |George Cheyne}}|title=Philosophical Principles of Religion
|passage=The heart beats, the blood circulates, the lungs '''play'''.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[bring]] into [[action]] or [[motion]]; to [[exhibit]] in action; to [[execute]] or [[deploy]].
#: {{ux|en|That was a great shot he '''played'''!}}
#: {{ux|en|He '''played''' the blue ball, but the green would have been a better choice.}}
#: {{ux|en|When you're in a team, you have to '''play''' your part.}}
#: {{ux|en|to '''play''' a trump in a card game, to '''play''' tricks, to '''play''' a joke}}
#* {{RQ:Milton Paradise Lost|book=V|passage=Nature here  /  Wantoned as in her prime, and '''played''' at will  /  Her virgin fancies.|year=1873}}
#* {{RQ:Rinehart Hopwood Bat|chapter=I|page=|passage=The Bat—they called him the Bat.{{nb...}}. He'd never been in stir, the bulls had never mugged him, he didn't run with a mob, he '''played''' a lone hand, and fenced his stuff so that even the fence couldn't swear he knew his face.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[handle]] or [[deal with]] (a [[matter]] or [[situation]]) in a stated way.
#: {{ux|en|The bank robbers have three hostages inside, so we're going to have to '''play''' this very carefully.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[handle]] or [[deal with]] (something) in a [[calculating]] [[manner]] [[intend]]ed to [[achieve]] [[profit]] or [[gain]].
#: {{ux|en|He made a fortune on Wall Street, '''playing''' the markets.}}
#: {{ux|en|In this business you have to '''play''' the percentages.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To be [[receive]]d or [[accept]]ed (in a given way); to [[go down]].
#: {{ux|en|This policy '''plays''' well with younger voters.}}
#: {{ux|en|How will this '''play''' in the swing states?}}
# To [[gamble]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1791|author={{w|Charlotte Smith (writer)|Charlotte Smith}}|title=Celestina|publisher=Broadview|year_published=2004|page=407
|passage=“I play, comparatively, very little; I don't drink a fifth part so much as half the people I live with; and I reckon myself, upon the whole, a very orderly, sober fellow.”}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[keep]] [[in play]], as a [[hook]]ed [[fish]] in order to [[land]] it.
# {{lb|en|transitive|colloquial}} To [[manipulate]], [[deceive]], or [[swindle]].
#: {{syn|en|defraud}}
#: {{ux|en|You '''played''' me!}}
# {{lb|en|AAVE|intransitive}} To [[kid]]; to [[joke]]; to [[say]] something for [[amusement]]; to [[act]], or to [[treat]] something, [[unseriously]].
#: {{ux|en|They don't '''play''' with the rules around here.}}
# <!--is this sense obsolete?-->{{lb|en|intransitive}} To take part in [[amorous]] activity; to [[make love]]; ''see also [[play around]]''.
#: {{syn|en|get it on|make out|have sex|Thesaurus:copulate}}
#* {{RQ:Spenser Faerie Queene|book=II|canto=IV|passage=Her proper face  /  I not descerned in that darkesome shade,  /  But weend it was my loue, with whom he '''playd'''.}}
#* {{quote-song|en|year=1977|album={{w|Suicide (1977 album)|Suicide}}|title=Cheree|artist={{w|Suicide (band)|Suicide}}|passage=Cheree, Cheree / Je t'adore, baby / I love you  / Oh, come '''play''' with me}}
# {{n-g|For additional senses in various idiomatic phrases, see the individual entries, such as '''[[play along]]''', '''[[play at]]''',  '''[[play down]]''', '''[[play off]]''', '''[[play on]]''', '''[[play out]]''', '''[[play to]]''', '''[[play up]]''', etc.}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun|~}}

# {{lb|en|uncountable|formerly|_|countable}} Activity for [[amusement]] only, especially among the young.
#: {{ux|en|Children learn through '''play'''.}}
#* {{RQ:Austen Northanger Abbey|text=She was fond of all boys' '''plays''', and greatly preferred cricket {{...}} to dolls {{...}}}}
# {{lb|en|uncountable}} Similar activity in young animals, as they explore their environment and learn new skills.
#: {{ux|en|This kind of '''play''' helps the young lion cubs develop their hunting skills.}}
# {{lb|en|uncountable}} The conduct, or course, of a game.
#: {{ux|en|'''Play''' was very slow in the first half.}}
#: {{ux|en|After the rain break, '''play''' resumed at 3 o'clock.}}
#: {{ux|en|The game was abandoned after 20 minutes' '''play'''}}
# {{lb|en|uncountable|sports|video games|with certain prepositions|also figurative}} The sphere or circumstance in which a playing implement, such as a ball, is played or available to be played (''see also'' [[in play]], [[out of play]]).
#: {{ux|en|In potting the yellow ball, he's knocked the green into '''play'''.}}
#: {{ux|en|When a chess piece is captured, it is removed from '''play'''.}}
#: {{ux|en|That option has been removed from '''play'''.}}
# {{lb|en|uncountable}} An individual's performance in a sport or game.
#: {{ux|en|His '''play''' has improved a lot this season.}}
# {{lb|en|countable}} A short sequence of action within a game.
#: {{ux|en|That was a great '''play''' by the Mudchester Rovers forward.}}
## {{lb|en|turn-based games}} An action carried out when it is one's turn to play.
##: {{syn|en|move}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=2009|author=Joe Edley; John Williams|title=Everything Scrabble: Third Edition|page=85
|passage=AWARD is better than either WARED or WADER. However, there's an even better '''play'''! If you have looked at the two-to-make-three letter list, you may have noticed the word AWA.}}
# {{senseid|en|literary composition for performance}} {{lb|en|countable}} A [[literary]] composition, intended to be represented by actors impersonating the characters and speaking the dialogue.
#: {{syn|en|drama|script<id:literary composition for performance>|Thesaurus:drama}}
#: {{hypo|en|screenplay|teleplay|telescript}}
#: {{ux|en|This book contains all of Shakespeare's '''plays'''.}}
# {{lb|en|countable}} A theatrical performance featuring [[actor]]s.
#: {{ux|en|We saw a two-act '''play''' in the theatre.}}
#: {{ux|en|My kids are acting in the school '''play''' this Christmas.}}
# {{lb|en|countable}} An attempt to move forward, as in a plan or strategy, for example by a business, investor, or political party.
#: {{ux|en|ABC Widgets makes a '''play''' in the bicycle market with its bid to take over Acme Sprockets.}}
#: {{ux|en|Turpin signals the Metric Party's long-term '''play''' for housing reform}}
# {{lb|en|countable}} A geological formation that contains an accumulation or prospect of hydrocarbons or other resources.
# {{lb|en|uncountable}} Movement (of a pattern of light etc.)
#: {{ux|en|the '''play''' of light and shadow across the boy's face}}
# {{lb|en|uncountable}} Freedom to move.
#: ''give '''play''' to your imagination''
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1954|year_published=1957|author=w:Ian Fleming|title={{w|Live and Let Die (novel)|Live and Let Die}}|volume=|location=London|publisher=Pan Books|chapter='Good Night To You Both'|page=223|passage=The negro came up and Bond allowed his arms to be tied behind his back. They were good knots. There was no '''play''' in them. They hurt.}}
## The extent to which a part of a mechanism can move freely, as for example [[lash]], [[backlash]], or [[slack]].
##: {{ux|en|No wonder the fanbelt is slipping: there’s too much '''play''' in it.}}
##: {{ux|en|Too much '''play''' in a steering wheel may be dangerous.}}
# {{lb|en|uncountable|informal}} {{U|sexual}} [[activity]] or sexual [[role-playing]].
#: {{coi|en|[[petplay|pet'''play''']]}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2014|author=Jiri T. Servant|title=Facts About Bondage - Bondage Guide For Beginners|passage=This type of '''play''' allows some people to relax and enjoy being given pleasure without having to think about giving pleasure back at the same time.}}
# {{lb|en|countable}} An instance of watching or listening to media.
#: {{syn|en|view|q1=of visual media|listen|q2=of audio}}
#: {{ux|en|That video of my cat falling off the piano has had ten thousand '''plays'''.}}
#* {{RQ:Time|author=Victor Luckerson|date=Dec 3 2014|title=These Were Spotify's Most-Streamed Songs This Year|passage=The most-streamed artist of the year was British singer Ed Sheeran, who amassed 860 million '''plays''' with hits like “I See Fire.”|url=https://time.com/3616091/spotify-most-streamed/|accessdate=7 August 2020|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170602140319/http://time.com/3616091/spotify-most-streamed/|archivedate=2 June 2017}}
# {{lb|en|countable|uncountable}} An instance or instances of causing media to be watched or heard, such as by broadcasting.
#: {{ux|en|Their single got a '''play''' on the radio.}}
#: {{ux|en|The song got a lot of '''play''' in the clubs.}}
# {{lb|en|countable}} A [[button]] that, when [[press]]ed, causes media to be played.
#: {{collocation|en|press '''play'''}}
# {{senseid|en|instance of wordplay}} {{lb|en|countable}} An instance of [[wordplay]].
#: {{m|en|'''play''' on words}}
#: {{ux|en|The name ''Wiktionary'' is a '''play''' on the words ''wiki'' and ''dictionary''.}}
# {{lb|en|archaic|now usually in compounds}} Activity relating to [[martial]] [[combat]] or [[fighting]].
#: {{m|en|hand'''play'''}}, {{m|en|sword'''play'''}}
